BESS Analysis Workbench — How to use
Viridi RPSLinkEX · Sunbelt Rentals · Internal tool

Standard workflow (have interval data)

  1. Tab 1 — Interval Data: drag-and-drop or open an XLSX/CSV meter export. The tool auto-detects columns, interval length, and kW vs kWh. Review the monthly table and worst-day chart. If the auto-detect is wrong, use the Override controls that appear.
  2. Tab 3 — Tariffs: enter or import 12 months of billed kW + demand $ from the utility bills. This sets the $/kW rate for savings calculations and enables the ratchet-aware model.
  3. Tab 2 — Sizing: the tool recommends a Viridi unit based on the worst-day demand profile. Review candidates, select a configuration, and adjust the peak target slider as needed.
  4. Tab 4 — Revenue: confirm which revenue streams apply — demand reduction, TOU arbitrage, DR. Enter DR $/kW-yr manually if the site has a program.
  5. Tab 5 — Deal Economics: set contract term, monthly service fee, and depreciation assumptions. Review the customer proposal snapshot and Sunbelt owner IRR/NPV.
  6. Tab 7 — Summary: print-ready proposal — shows site profile, recommended unit, savings, and the pro-forma cashflow table.

No interval data? (bill-only or ComStock proxy)

Two options when you only have monthly invoices and no meter CSV/XLSX:

  • Bill-only mode: go straight to Tab 3 — Tariffs and enter 12 months of billed kW + demand $. The tool runs a conservative sizing using a worst-day duration assumption that scales with the peak's size (3-5h). Results are flagged as indicative.
  • ComStock proxy: on Tab 1 — Interval Data, scroll down past the file-drop area to the ComStock Building Profile card. Pick the building type closest to your site (office, retail, warehouse, restaurant, light manufacturing) and click Generate. This synthesizes a representative 8,760-hr load shape from the NREL ComStock database, scaled to your billed kW from the Tariffs tab. Once generated, all tabs (sizing, dispatch, savings) work exactly as with real interval data. Flag all proxy outputs as indicative screening — not site-specific.
  • ComStock requires billed kW in the Tariffs tab first — add those before clicking Generate.

What each tab does

1. Interval DataImport + analyze 15-min meter data. Year overview + monthly peaks + worst-day profile charts. Heat map shows seasonal demand patterns.
2. SizingRecommends Viridi RPSLinkEX configuration. Shows all unit/count candidates with monthly capture rates and the Peak Target Finder sweep.
3. TariffsMonthly billed kW + demand $/kW. Sets billing-floor % (ratchet). Reference rate library for market presets (NY, CA, TX, MA, CT).
4. RevenueValue stack by revenue stream. Enter DR estimate and toggle TOU arbitrage. Shows total annual cash benefit feeding into economics.
5. Deal EconomicsCustomer proposal snapshot + Sunbelt owner pro-forma. ITC, bonus depreciation, contract term, residual value, IRR / NPV / payback.
6. CA TOUFor SCE / SDG&E sites: every-interval dispatch simulation. NC + on-peak demand reduction + TOU arbitrage, no ratchet floor.
7. SummaryPrint-ready customer-facing proposal. Export via the Print button in the top bar.

Key concepts

Billing floor (ratchet)The utility bills the GREATER of this month's actual peak or ~70% of your highest peak in the rolling past 12 months — a floor that ratchets up with each new peak and holds for a year (they reserved capacity for your biggest spike). Two upshots: you can't save below the floor (so naive peak-minus-average estimates run ~2–4× high), and shaving your single highest peak lowers the floor for ALL 12 months. The tool always uses this ratchet model. PSEG-LI Rate 281 ≈ 70% (bill-validated); >145 kW classes can be ~85%.
Peak target (kW)The kW ceiling the battery holds your billed peak under. Lower target = more shaving = more savings, until the required shave exceeds what the battery can physically deliver on the worst day of the month.
Capture of demand $What share of the site's annual demand charges a configuration recovers when every month is shaved to the deepest level it can sustainably hold (worst day of the month governs). The ratchet billing floor caps how deep any configuration can go.
Worst-day dispatchSavings are governed by the worst day of each month, not an average day. Averaging days overstates savings ~2.6× (confirmed in Viridi PC146 analysis for this dataset). The tool always dispatches against the worst day.
Round-trip efficiencyCharge efficiency × discharge efficiency ≈ 88% for Viridi units (94% each way). This means 1 kWh drawn from the grid stores 0.94 kWh, delivering 0.88 kWh net. Dispatch math applies this correctly — naive models often ignore it.
